Resolves #18316

Workstation gets Undo and Redo, and they are the Group's rather than the app's.

The topology bar's two new actions read the Group's own provider leaf where it lives. `state.Provider#getData` resolves to that leaf's `core.Config`, so a formatter running inside a binding effect registers it and re-runs when it changes — the enablement is reactive without a copy, a subscription, or any change to the provider chain. Handlers are a bare manager dispatch. The consumer keeps no stack, mirrors no cursor, and re-derives nothing per commit.

**This leaf touches no engine file.** Undo and Redo are the Group's, and the app binds to state the engine already publishes.

Evidence: L3 (real Chrome, real popup, real native window move, real Neural Link command over the shared cursor) → L3 required (AC-1/2/3). **Outside-CI, author-run: the e2e suite runs in no CI workflow — by design per #14685, whose execution arm is a host-side runner I could not confirm live from this seat. These are one-time observations with named controls, not a standing guard.** Residual: none for this ticket; the follow-up below is #18314's, not this leaf's.

## What this PR adds, and what it deliberately does not

Most of #18316's criteria were already satisfied by its prerequisites when I picked it up. I swept for that before building, and it changed the work: the capstone's job is the **controls**, the **two ordering arms**, and a **ledger** — not a second implementation of what #18307, #18308, #18311, #18313 and #18315 already delivered.

Two of my own claims in that sweep were wrong and were retracted publicly before this PR opened. I reported `history.count` as asserted nowhere and AC-4's identity set as uncovered; both were artefacts of grepping my vocabulary instead of the tree's (`historyCount`, `getPaneIdentity`). The table reflects what is actually there.

| Per-window live-layout persistence | **#18308** (`ec5eb923da`) | `dashboard/dock/model/Persistence.mjs` hard-cut to keyed workspace records (−122). **Zero `windowId` references remain under `src/dashboard/dock/persistence/`.** |

Two `syncDock*` names survive and are deliberately not sweeps, recorded so the ledger does not read as an oversight: `syncDockLockPane` (14 references) is the bound lock-presentation seam, `syncDockProjection` (5) a plugin hook. Neither re-derives presentation per commit.

## Deltas from ticket

**The arms extend `WorkstationTopologyGroupsNL.spec.mjs` rather than adding a journey file.** The ticket says "add one permanent multi-window Neural Link journey"; that journey exists, and its boot, pop-out and Group-state helpers are the ones these arms need. A second file would have duplicated ~150 lines of fixture to assert against the same Group.

**AC-7 was narrowed in the ticket body** on operator scope direction of 2026-09-06: one main window with popups is this epic's multi-window story; a second *independent* main window is an edge case kept outside #18303 and #18304. #18284's cross-root isolation implementation shipped and stays; only its rendered receipt defers, owned by #18379.

**The engine seam was withdrawn during review.** Earlier heads added `bindGroupHistoryState` and a retirement listener to `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs`. Neither survives: the delivered shape needs no engine change at all, so that file is untouched and its size baseline is unchanged. `unit/dashboard/DockGroupHistoryBinding.spec.mjs` retired with it — accounted for in the commit, its live half moved to the controller spec where the code now lives.

**Two commits were dropped before this PR opened** because #18314 carries the same decisions and its lane needs them: the Workstation history depth (its `dockHistoryDepth` config supersedes my `static HISTORY_DEPTH`) and the `preserveItemIds` union (#18383 carries the hunk verbatim). Both were mine first and both are better placed there.

## Test Evidence

CI-covered (`npm run test-unit`): `unit/dashboard` + `unit/apps/workstation` — **979 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed** at `19642a9adf`.

Outside-CI, run with `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT=<neo-agent-brain>` and `npx playwright test -c test/playwright/playwright.config.e2e.mjs --workers=1`:

- `e2e/workstation/WorkstationTopologyGroupsNL.spec.mjs --grep "ordered rows|ONE cursor"` — **2 passed**, normal exit; the AC-2 arm re-run **3× at ~3.9s** after its flake repair.
- `--grep "cold active selection"` — **1 passed, 25.2s**, normal exit.

Every arm was run against a control, and one control changed the work rather than confirming it:

| arm | control | result |
|---|---|---|
| AC-2 ordered rows | CDP move suppressed | fails on its own message after the full 30s poll |
| AC-3 shared cursor | invert which item is expected reversed | fails |
| AC-6 empty log | cold hydrate `cursorAction` → `append` | fails on the pre-existing empty-history assertion |

**The AC-2 arm was reshaped twice, both times by a control.** Its first version asserted `historyCount` reached 2 after the move, passed in 1.6s — and passed *with the move suppressed*, because popping out appends rows of its own. Green while witnessing nothing. The replacement counted from a settled baseline instead, which turned it into a race with those same rows: it failed once at 31.7s and passed at 4.2s on re-run with no code change. The delivered arm counts nothing. It polls for a row whose `cause` is `native-popup-move`, which has exactly one producer, so neither a stale baseline nor a settle race can manufacture it. **3/3 runs at ~3.9s**, and the suppressed-move control still fails on its own message.


## Post-Merge Validation

None outstanding for this ticket's criteria. Two things are true after merge and belong to other owners:

- The e2e arms here run in no CI workflow, by design (#14685). They are author-run observations with named controls; if the host-side runner is confirmed live they become a standing guard, and if it is not, that is a fact about every L3 row in both epics' matrices rather than about this PR.
- `PopupWorkspace` mounts no `DockDropIndicators` — see Follow-up. It does not affect any criterion above.

## Follow-up (not this PR)

`PopupWorkspace` mounts no `DockDropIndicators` — three mount sites on `dev` before #18314, one after, and none in the new owner. A committed full popup therefore presents no drop affordances, a capability the bare vessel had. Raised in my #18383 review and owned there; it does not block this leaf's criteria.
